chunks.arabic_text: وَسَأَلَ سَمَاعَةُ بْنُ مِهْرَانَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: عَنْ لُحُومِ السِّبَاعِ مِنَ الطَّيْرِ وَالدَّوَابِّ قَالَ

translations.en: Samaʿah ibn Mihrān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the meat of predatory animals among birds and beasts. He said:

chunks.arabic_text: «أَمَّا أَكْلُ لَحْمِهَا فَإِنَّا نَكْرَهُهُ وَأَمَّا الْجُلُودُ فَارْكَبُوا عَلَيْهَا وَلَا تَلْبَسُوا مِنْهَا شَيْئًا تُصَلُّونَ فِيهِ.»

translations.en: "As for eating their meat, we dislike it; and as for the skins, ride upon them, but do not wear anything made from them in which you perform salat (prayer)."

en.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on predatory animals among birds and beasts. It states that eating their meat is disliked, while their skins may be used for riding or similar utility, but they are not to be worn in salat (prayer).
en.seo_question: Can the skins of predatory animals be used or worn during salat (prayer)?

key_terms.لُحُومِ: meats; referring here to the flesh of predatory animals
key_terms.السِّبَاعِ: predatory animals or beasts of prey
key_terms.الطَّيْرِ: birds; here, predatory birds are included
key_terms.الدَّوَابِّ: beasts or animals that move upon the earth
key_terms.نَكْرَهُهُ: we dislike it; indicating karāhah in this context
key_terms.فَارْكَبُوا: then ride upon; use them for riding or similar utility
